cases.name: First deployment to D environment
cases.input: Deploy a trained LightGBM model to the dev (D) environment for the first time.
expected_behaviors: Creates an online endpoint if it does not exist
Uses az ml online-deployment create with --all-traffic flag to route 100% traffic to new deployment
Follows D → Q → P promotion sequence (starts at D, does not skip to Q)
Names the deployment following the model registry naming convention (e.g. my_model_v1)
References the scoring script with the correct PYTHONPATH (aml/pipeline/src)
should_not: Omit --all-traffic on first deployment (would leave 0% traffic to the new deployment)
Skip D and deploy directly to Q or P
Use az ml online-endpoint create for re-deploying to an existing endpoint

cases.name: Update existing endpoint without duplicate deployment
cases.input: I need to update an inference endpoint with a retrained model. The endpoint already exists.
expected_behaviors: Uses az ml online-deployment update (not create) since the endpoint already exists
Warns that az ml online-deployment create on an existing endpoint creates a second deployment at 0% traffic
Verifies traffic allocation after the update
Runs a smoke test against the endpoint after deployment
should_not: Use az ml online-deployment create on an already-deployed endpoint
Assume the existing deployment will be replaced automatically without traffic reallocation

cases.name: Promotion from Q to P
cases.input: The model passed QA testing. How do I promote it to production?
expected_behaviors: Triggers the Azure DevOps deploy-inference pipeline targeting the P environment branch
Confirms the Q endpoint health-check passed before initiating P deployment
References the endpoint_inference.yml and deployment_inference.yml from aml/mlops/definitions/
Notes that P promotion requires explicit approval gate in the ADO pipeline
should_not: Deploy directly to P without referencing the Q validation result
Manually run az ml online-deployment create against the P workspace without going through the ADO pipeline

cases.name: Blue-green deployment with traffic splitting
cases.input: Deploy a new model version alongside the current one with 20% traffic to the new deployment for canary testing.
expected_behaviors: Creates a second deployment on the same endpoint with --traffic 20
Leaves the existing deployment at 80% traffic
Does not use --all-traffic flag (would route 100% to new deployment, defeating canary purpose)
Reports both deployment names and their traffic percentages after creation
Provides the scoring URI which routes traffic according to the split
should_not: Use --all-traffic on the canary deployment (would cut off traffic to the stable deployment)
Create a separate endpoint for the canary deployment
Forget to verify that both deployments show provisioningState=Succeeded

cases.name: Pre-deployment validation checklist
cases.input: Before deploying my model, run through the pre-deployment validation checklist.
expected_behaviors: Confirms Azure login and correct subscription with az account show
Verifies the model exists in the registry with az ml model list
Runs unit tests: pytest tests/unit/ --verbose --tb=short
Runs component argument validation if pipeline YAML was changed: pytest tests/integration/test_component_argument_validation.py -v
Runs scoring script edge-case test: python aml/api/test_score_local.py
Reports pass/fail status for each checklist item
should_not: Proceed with deployment if any checklist item fails
Skip unit tests because 'the model was already tested during training'
Assume the scoring script works without running test_score_local.py

cases.name: Endpoint health check post-deployment
cases.input: The deployment just finished. Check that the endpoint is healthy and responding correctly.
expected_behaviors: Checks endpoint provisioningState is 'Succeeded' via az ml online-endpoint show
Checks all deployments on the endpoint have provisioningState='Succeeded'
Retrieves recent deployment logs with az ml online-deployment get-logs
Scans logs for error patterns: OutOfMemoryError, ConnectionRefused, Timeout, OOMKilled, CRASH, FATAL
Invokes the endpoint with a test payload via az ml online-endpoint invoke
Validates the response is non-null JSON with predictions in expected range
Reports response latency and confirms it is under 2s for single-row payload
should_not: Consider the deployment successful if only the endpoint state is Succeeded but deployments are still provisioning
Skip log scanning — a deployment can be provisioned but failing on every request
Accept a null or empty response from the endpoint invocation as healthy
